title: Adopter lightweight playmap and first-week checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playmap for small engineering teams trying Redwood SDK for the first week. Goal is to get a working demo, basic telemetry flowing, and clear escalation/fallback guidance without pages of theory. Keep this in a pocket (<= 1 page when printed).

Audience:
- Integrators: product engineers embedding Redwood in a feature prototype
- Platform buddies/SEs: internal SE who will support the first 2-3 adopters
- Solutions engineers running the first demo with a customer

High-level outcomes by EOW (end of week 1):
1) Sample app integrated with Redwood SDK (local dev or sandbox).
2) Basic auth + env propagation validated.
3) Telemetry events (request.success, request.latency_ms, model.fallback) emitted to sandbox observability.
4) Smoke tests pass (generation, streaming chunk, embeddings).
5) Rollback/fallback plan rehearsed (local model stub or alternative endpoint).

Quickprep (15–30m) before pairing/demo:
- Create API key in Console sandbox (team account), add to .env.local as REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Clone starter repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/starter-embed.git && cd starter-embed
- Check Node/Python runtime versions in README; install deps: npm ci or pip -r requirements.txt.
- Run dev server locally: npm run dev or python -m http.server 3000 (follow repo README).

First-hour checklist (fast-path):
- Replace sample call with a tiny gen call: send prompt "Summarize: <one-line>". Validate 200 and text output.
- Test streaming on a small prompt; confirm chunking arrives.
- Create one embedding call and verify vector length matches model doc.
- If any call fails, run curl against the API with the same key to rule out SDK bug: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"input":"hi"}'

Telemetry gating (basic probe events to ship quickly):
- Names and minimal schema (string tags allowed):
  - request.attempt [tags: route, model_variant, env]
  - request.success [tags: route, model_variant, latency_bucket]
  - request.latency_ms (numeric) [tags: route, model_variant]
  - model.fallback.triggered [tags: original_model, fallback_model, reason]
  - integration.smoke_test.passed [tags: step]
- Thresholds to watch for first week:
  - error rate > 5% over 1h -> page on-call SRE
  - 95p latency > advertised SLA for demo route -> notify eng-developer-experience
  - Any model.fallback.triggered -> record context, file a Jira INF ticket

Smoke tests (local quick suite) - run in CI and locally:
- test_generate_basic: one-shot generation returns non-empty text
- test_streaming_chunks: receives >1 chunk for prompt length >64 tokens
- test_embedding_shape: returns vector length expected
- test_auth_error: missing key returns 401
- test_rate_limit_header: if service returns 429, SDK surface exposes retry-after header
Implementation note: these are intentionally shallow to catch integration regressions, not hallucinations.

Demo scripts (30 min demo flow):
- 0–5m: Context + slide on what Redwood solves (latency/cost/rollouts)
- 5–10m: Live code: replace sample key, run small gen, show response text
- 10–15m: Toggle to streaming mode and show progressive tokens arriving
- 15–20m: Trigger a simulated error (flip key to invalid) to show how the app surfaces errors and safe fallback copy
- 20–25m: Show telemetry dashboard with the request.attempt and request.latency_ms spikes from the demo (use pre-populated data if possible)
- 25–30m: Next steps and onboarding link posted to customer in Slack

Fallbacks + incident play (practical):
- If the hosted endpoint is degraded: switch SDK config to point at dedicated sandbox or use the local stub runner (repo has ./stubs/local-stub.sh).
- If a model variant causes quality regression: pin model to previous variant in env var: REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-1.0-legacy
- If errors persist >30m during demo: gracefully degrade to cached replies (check cache/prefix store) and resume demo talking through offline evaluation plan.

Minimal docs to hand to adopter (1–2 pages):
- 1-liner: what the SDK does and quick call example (python/node)
- Quick checklist: env, run, smoke tests, telemetry checks
- Escalation contacts + Slack channel: #dx-adopters, #sre-oncall
- Links: console quickstart, SDK reference, PR that added sample app

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Add a tiny network emulation script for showing latency buckets (INF-XXX task)
- Decide canonical telemetry event names with SRE (currently ad-hoc above) -> ACTION: book 30m with @Liam
- Make the smoke tests part of the starter repo CI matrix and gate on passing before issuing sandbox keys to customers
- Draft a 1-page PDF to hand to sales that matches this flow (low effort)

Quick troubleshooting tips (common gotchas):
- 401 on first try: confirm key copied correctly; some terminals strip characters when copying from Console; try quoting the key in .env
- Streaming shows blank chunks: check Accept header and SDK streaming flag; confirm server supports chunked streaming on the route
- Embedding vector dims mismatch: double-check model name; some models have 1536 vs 1024 dims
- Local stub failing: run ./stubs/init.sh to regenerate test vectors

Short follow-up plan after week 1:
- Day 8: brief async retro with adopter (what worked/what broke) + add telemetry gaps to backlog
- Week 2: enable longer eval runs and tie to Optimize suggestions (quantization/batching) if cost is a blocker
- Week 3: propose Dedicated trial if throughput/cost estimates justify

Slack copy template to send to new adopter (pasteable):
"Hi @channel :wave: welcome! Quick starter checklist in this doc: <drive link>. First quicksteps: add REDWOOD_API_KEY to your env, run npm ci, then npm run dev and paste a screenshot of your first successful gen. If you hit anything, ping #dx-adopters or DM Maya.

"

Notes: keep this file short and iterate. This is intentionally conversational and full of small todo markers. If you repurpose anything for an external customer PDF, remove internal links and ticket references first.

Last edited by: Maya Chen (eng-developer-experience)
